Issue: [#2022](https://github.com/openagt/openagent/issues/2022)

# Automations: skills bring the scheduled rows, each person sets when they run

## TLDR

A project's scheduled commands stop being lines of a hand-written `agent-schedule.md`. A command skill says in its own `SKILL.md` that it can be scheduled, with its check and its default pace, so an installed skill adds its own row. Each person sets the rest per repository: whether the row runs, its pace (down to a time of day), and how far its runs publish. A new Automations page shows and sets the rows.

## Why it matters

- A line can name a skill the project does not have. Its row still shows, looks switched on, and never starts; the reason ("no such command in this project") is only on the Overview card.
- Adding a row means editing a file. A check is a long shell line: this repository's are 200 to 500 characters each, mostly `jq`.
- The check lives far from the skill it belongs to. Whoever brings a skill into a 
… 3448 characters cut …
oth. Is that fine?
4. An unknown `schedule` key in a skill file must be harmless to Claude Code and to Codex. To check before building.
5. The scheduler looks for a command under `.claude/skills` only. The launcher reads `.agents/skills` too. The rows should be read from both.
6. A row set to 10:00 when the scheduler is not running at 10:00 (the dashboard closed, the laptop asleep) or has no quota then. Proposed: start it once, when the scheduler next can, and never twice for one missed day.
7. Saying in words what a row waits for. A check is a shell line, so the page cannot turn it into a sentence. To show "when there are merged pull requests to write up", the skill has to give that short line beside its check. Without it the page can only say "when its check finds work".
8. This reverses a written decision. `packages/agent-scheduler/DECISIONS.md` says the schedule is a tracked file a person writes, and that a line is the team's default. That text has to be rewritten by a person.

## Not part of this

- A new project has no scheduler: the package is not one of the built-in ones, so the page shows only where a project installed it. What a new project gets by default is a question of its own.
- A person's own prompt as an automation. It fits later as an "Add" button on the page that saves the prompt as a command skill, which then has a row like any other. Such a row runs by a time. A check is optional there: a shell line the person types, kept with the command like any skill's check, and only a row that has one is offered "whenever there is work".

## Cost

The scheduler package: how it reads the rows, its state, its command line, its part of the dashboard. The five scheduled skills each gain their lines (six rows, `triage` has two). This repository's `agent-schedule.md` is deleted.

# Agent schedule

One line per command. The command is written as a person types it, without the slash: the name of a skill folder under `.claude/skills/`, then at most one word the skill takes as its argument (`triage quick`); each such line is its own command, with its own pace and switch. `every` is how often at most: the command is due only once that long has passed since its last recorded start. `when` is a check, run at the repository root: the command is due while the check exits 0 and prints a JSON value that is not empty (or any text that is not JSON). A line carries one or both; with both, an agent starts only when both hold. `cap` is how many runs of the command may be in flight at once, across every machine that shares this repository; 1 when absent. `off` lists a command that runs only on a machine where a person switched it on (Settings → Scheduler, or `npx agent-scheduler switch <command> on`, the command quoted when it has a word after it); every other command runs unless a person switched it off on that machine. `publish` says how far a run of the command publishes its work: `commit` it and push nothing, push its `branch`, open its `pr`, or set the pull request to `merge` on its own once its checks pass; a line that says nothing publishes nothing. That is the default on every machine: a person may pick another level for a command on their own machine (Settings → Scheduler, or `npx agent-scheduler publish <command> <nothing|commit|branch|pr|merge>`, and `file` in its place to follow the line again).

I'm still unsure whether an unknown schedule key is actually harmless to Claude Code and Codex—I believe Claude Code ignores unrecognized frontmatter keys, but I can't fully confirm that.

Codex seems to follow a similar pattern, recognizing name/description plus a metadata field while ignoring other keys, and the Agent Skills spec does define metadata as a string-to-string map for arbitrary data. The plan for the Automations ticket (issue #2022) is written and saved as `tickets/2026-10-08_automations-skills-bring-scheduled-rows.plan.md`. The queue entry is marked done, my claim is released, and the ticket stays open. No file in the checkout changed, so there is no commit, push or pull request.

The plan rates the work at effort 6 and uncertainty 5. Two things in it need you before the work can merge:

- **`DECISIONS.md` rewrite:** the scheduler's written decisions say the schedule is a tracked file, and reject a clock time of day. The plan has the pull request propose the new bullets for you to write in.
- **Rows start off:** the plan takes the ticket's proposal that every row starts switched off and publishes nothing until a person picks. That stops the four rows that run by default in this repository today (`work-queue`, `update-tickets`, `plan-tickets`, `triage quick`) until each is switched on again.

How the plan answers the ticket's other open questions:

- **Cap:** it stays with the skill, since it counts runs across machines.
- **Publish default:** it leaves the skill; whoever switches a row on picks how far it publishes.
- **Two rows from one skill:** a row may carry an `argument`, so `triage quick` and `triage consensual` keep their names.
- **Missed time of day:** the row starts once when the scheduler next can; no extra state is needed.
- **Skill folders:** rows are read from both `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills`.
- **What a row waits for:** an optional short `waits` line beside the check.

I did not test whether an unknown `schedule` key in a skill's front matter is harmless to Claude Code and Codex. The plan makes that the first step, with a `schedule.yml` file beside `SKILL.md` as the fallback.
